thread:
Marta: Heads-up — I'm about to push a small terraform change to switch svc/api from ClusterIP -> NodePort so we can attach an NLB for passthrough TLS. Quick question: do we need to map the TLS secret ARN onto the Gateway API TLS config, or does our ALB/NLB passthrough rely purely on Ingress annotations?
Ryan: For NLB passthrough we usually do TCP passthrough at L4, so the cert stays on the backend pod. If you want the Gateway (ALB) to terminate TLS you map the cert to the GatewayHTTPRoute/Listener. NLB TLS listener can also have ACM certs attached.
Marta: Got it. The reason I'm asking is svc/api is behind the grpc-proxy pod that does SNI-based routing. We're seeing some fallback where unknown SNI hits the default cert and the proxy rejects. Wondering if we should wire a default TLS secret into the Gateway so SNI fallback gets a valid cert instead of the proxy 525s.
Devon: Can you paste the current Service + Gateway YAML?
Marta: Sure — current service (we're templating via terraform k8s_manifest):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: api
  namespace: prod
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  ports:
    - name: tcp-ssl
      port: 443
      targetPort: 8443
  selector:
    app: api
```
And the Gateway fragment that frontends prod cluster:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.x-k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: prod-gw
  namespace: infra
spec:
  gatewayClassName: redwood-aws-gw
  listeners:
    - name: https
      protocol: TLS
      port: 443
      tls:
        mode: Terminate
        certificateRefs:
          - name: prod-alb-cert
```
Marta: So currently Gateway terminates TLS (Terminate) but we expect NodePort+NLB passthrough in this change which would bypass Gateway termination. That mismatch might be why proxy sees default certs.
Ryan: Two things to consider: 1) If you convert service -> NodePort and register nodes to NLB with target type instance, the NLB can be configured with TLS passthrough (NLB TLS listener -> target group with instance protocol TLS). In that case Gateway shouldn't terminate (mode: Passthrough) — update tls.mode. 2) If you want a predictable fallback cert, add a certificateRef pointing to a secret with SANs for the default host, or attach ACM cert to the NLB listener.
Samir: Another gotcha: when using SNI routing in the proxy you need to ensure the K8s Service preserves the original destination port and that the backend is expecting TLS. If terraform changes the targetPort, svc selector, or nodePort range, healthchecks can flip and cause 525s.
Marta: Thanks. One more thing — infra-bot issued a warning on the TF plan about changing service annotations. It suggested migrating from "service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: tcp" to the Gateway API config. Do we have a migration doc?
Infra-bot: [deploy-check] Detected service type change: ClusterIP -> NodePort. Review: security group rules, nodePort range (30000-32767), and NLB target registration.
Devon: We don't have a full migration doc for this exact pattern. Quick checklist I'd follow: update Service.type, add nodePort in manifest (or let k8s pick), update terraform aws_lb_target_group to use target_type=instance and protocol=TLS if passthrough; if terminating on ALB/GW then set gateway tls.mode=Terminate and ensure cert refs are valid. Also update health check protocol to TCP/TLS as appropriate.
Ryan: For Gateway API, to keep compatibility you can set listener.tls.mode = Passthrough and then in the HTTPRoute/GatewayRoute do SNI matching. If you need default cert, you either 1) switch to Terminate and use cert on the Gateway, or 2) attach ACM cert on NLB.
Marta: Ok plan: I'll patch the TF to add nodePort + set aws_lb_target_group.protocol = "TLS" and change the Gateway listener to Passthrough for this service only as a canary. I'll also add a default secret mapping to gateway tls.certificateRefs to reduce unknown SNI failures in case of misrouting. Ping me for a quick review before applying.
Samir: Recommend also adding a small smoke test job that performs an SNI handshake to each hostname and verifies cert SAN before and after deploy.
Marta: Will do. Thanks all — I'll drop the PR in ~15m and tag @ryan @devon for review. :thumbsup:
Ryan: SGTM. Keep an eye on healthcheck flips.
Devon: Lmk when PR is up, I'll run smoke tests. :eyes:
